summary: 8. Having heard the representatives of the Petitioner and after perusing the material **(iii)** The respondents have submitted that the claims of delay on account of the Citizenship Amendment Bill and Law & Order issues are liable to be rejected. Generalized statements have been made by the Petitioner without demonstrating how the project was impacted due to the same. Additionally, reasons like remoteness of location, unavailability of skilled labour, and problems in bringing labour from other States because of the Inter Labour Permit (ILP) cannot be considered as unforeseen circumstances. The Petitioner, having experience of several decades in the field, should have contemplated such labour issues at the time of planning the project itself and should have taken steps to alleviate the possible difficulties well in advance. The alleged incidents of threatening in the adjacent location and the alleged bandh of 80 days too cannot be considered as circumstances that would unreasonably delay the project. **(v)** Regarding ROW issues, the Respondents have submitted that in the instant Petition, it is mentioned that immediate actions were initiated with respect to the survey work of the transmission lines; further, the concerned authority was also intimated regarding the upcoming project. The Petitioner has claimed that issues were encountered from the start of transmission line work during stages of preliminary survey, line plotting, etc.; however, the said claims are without any details and supporting documents. Further, having known about the various RoW issues to be encountered, the Petitioner has not provided documentary proof regarding the remedial measures it took for the same. Out of the 206 locations tabulated by the Petitioner where RoW issues were allegedly faced by them, the majority of them (131 locations, i.e., after serial no. 75) pertain to the period after the SCOD of 15.1.2018, and the steps taken thereafter should be explained by the Petitioner. Additionally, the delay claimed on account of alleged RoW issues is exorbitant and liable to be rejected. Time being consumed for resolving RoW issues ought to be in contemplation of the Petitioner, the same being usually encountered in construction projects; as per the Petitioner itself, the issues at several locations (over 80) were resolved in under 50 days. The Petitioner should demonstrate the quantum of land affected to explain the huge delay occasioned. 39. We have gone through the documents placed on record and observed that the Petitioner has claimed the delay due to violent protests erupted in Assam from 4 th December 2019 to March 2020, and due to various bands organized by extremist groups. However, it is observed that the Petitioner has failed to furnish any documentation substantiating the purported delay in the construction activity due to the aforementioned violent protest that erupted in Assam. Also, the Petitioner has not provided the documentary evidence for the efforts made to reduce the impact on the construction activities and the exact timelines wherein the implementation of the project was affected due to aforementioned issues. Therefore, given the lack of supporting evidence, the Commission is unable to exercise its discretion to condone the aforementioned delay on account of the CAA protest. However, the Petitioner is at liberty to approach the Commission at the time of truing up with the valid documentary evidence against the effect of CAA protest on the construction activities at a particular location of T/L, and the same will be reviewed at the time of truing up. 41. We have observed that the Petitioner has claimed the delay of around 80 days of bandhs from the date of initial start of the construction of the project. However, it is observed that the Petitioner has failed to furnish any evidentiary substantiation or documentation substantiating the purported delay in the construction activity due to the aforementioned Law and Order situation. Also, the Petitioner has not provided the documentary evidence for the efforts made to reduce the impact on the construction activities and the exact timelines wherein the implementation of the project was affected due to aforementioned issues. Therefore, given the lack of supporting evidence, the Commission is unable to exercise its discretion to condone the delay of 80 days on account of Law & Order issues. However, the Petitioner is at liberty to approach the Commission at the time of truing up with the valid documentary evidence against the effect of Law & order issues on the construction activities at a particular location of T/L, and the same will be reviewed at the time of truing up. demanding high baseless compensation. Due to such sensitive issues, proper handling of these cases was necessary, and this led to a delay in the completion of work in these sections. The Petitioner has also submitted that a Petition was filed by an influential businessman having a strong political backup with the ruling party, in the Court of Civil Judge, Kokrajhar, for granting a temporary injunction against the highway crossing area, Serfanguri on 9.5.2019. As a result,no work could be done in that section until and unless the court case was resolved. 48. Per contra, the Respondent has submitted that, having known about the various RoW issues to be encountered, the Petitioner has not stated about and given documentary proof regarding the mitigation or remedial measures it took at the outset. The delay claimed on account of RoW issues is exorbitant and liable to be rejected 98. This order disposes of Petition No. 45/TT/2023 in terms of the above findings and discussions.
